title: Dormancy of Savings and Money Market Accounts, and the Return to Active Status
content:
### What counts as customer-initiated activity

On an account of Savings & Money Market Accounts, customer-initiated activity means a deposit or a withdrawal the owner makes at a branch, at an ATM, by mobile deposit, by online, mobile or telephone transfer, by money market check or by wire. Interest credits, fees, refunds, ACH credits, automatic transfers and overdraft protection transfers are not customer-initiated. The account carries the date of the latest such activity.

### When an account becomes dormant

An active account becomes dormant once the tier's dormancy period in calendar months has passed after the last customer-initiated activity. Calendar months are counted from the date of that last activity, and the account is due for dormancy when the current date is on or after that date plus the tier's dormancy period in calendar months, falling back to the last day of the month where that day does not exist. The comparison is not-earlier-than, so the day the period is reached itself satisfies it.

### While the account is dormant

The tier's dormant account fee is assessed at each cycle close, carrying the dormant account fee code. The fee is reduced so that it never takes the balance below zero, and it is not written at all on a zero balance. No maintenance fee is assessed in a dormant cycle. Interest continues to accrue while the account is dormant.

### Returning to active status

The identity of the owner must be verified before a dormant account is reactivated. Reactivation needs a customer-initiated transaction in the same contact, and the date of that transaction becomes the new date of last customer activity.

### Boundary of the dormancy period

Take a hypothetical account on a tier whose dormancy period is 24 calendar months, whose last customer-initiated activity fell on 14 June. The account is not due for dormancy on 13 June two years later, and is due on 14 June two years later and on every day after it, until a customer-initiated transaction resets the date.
